title: Public Operational Evidence Pointer
description: Closed, data-minimized pointer to privately custodied operational evidence. Validity proves only persistence and verified remote readback.

remote_readback.description: OBSERVED outcome of the remote readback. Pinning this to `const: "verified"` made the field carry no information: every conforming pointer asserted success, a failed or skipped readback was unrepresentable, and the claim could be manufactured by anyone able to author a conforming file. NOTE the residual gap — an enum makes the outcome falsifiable but still self-reported. Binding it to independently authenticable evidence (verifier identity plus a signed verification-receipt digest, keeping object location private) requires the signer and validator tracked in `_meta.enforcement_status`; consumers MUST NOT treat this field as proof until then.

claim_ceiling.description: Does not prove current health, authorization, placement, software versions, topology, failures, recovery-artifact hashes, provider or object location, or secret state.

_meta.purpose: Publish a content digest and remote-readback fact without publishing operational receipt metadata or location.
_meta.enforcement_status: NOT YET ENFORCED. No validator in this repository checks any instance against this schema, so `$schema` here is a declaration of intent rather than a constraint. Three bindings await the owned Rust validator: (1) instance-against-schema validation, (2) digest-to-filename binding, (3) authentication of `remote_readback` against a signed verification receipt. Until (3) lands the readback outcome is self-reported and is not evidence.
